name: Traffic-weighted scoring + land screen as warnings + redevelopment corner
notes: Thresholds and weights PROPOSED until Ross approves after the backtest and his blind review.

tiers.pool: corners passing the v1.1 land screen

backtest.run: 2026-11-17 on rebuilt data (rebuilt v1.0 reproduces the published scores at r=0.996; backtest 76th pct, 51% top quarter vs 76/54% published)

v1.2 weights + signal unknown 0.25 (not.why_not: new 7-Elevens are often on county roads FDOT doesn't track for signals; quarter credit pushed them down

scope_approved: Ross, 2026-11-17: build items 1 (land screen as warnings, rail/houses warnings), 2 (traffic weights, after backtest), 3 (signal unknown at quarter credit; tested, not adopted: see backtest), 4 (redevelopment corner per trade area), 5 (7-Eleven data gap at #27) from Luke's full review; Ross (not Jacob) does the blind review.

changes: 1. Scoring now leans on traffic: traffic 35 points (was 25), new homes 25 (was 30), gap to the nearest 7-Eleven 5 (was 10). In Luke's 50 answers, traffic separated his Yes from his No; new homes didn't, because every corner on the list already has strong growth.

2. The land screen warns instead of removing. Only competitor/7-Eleven/rail/utility-owned parcels and parcels with less than 1.0 acre near the corner are removed. Mapped wetlands, a parcel with under 1.3 upland acres, a parcel on one road only, a rail line at the parcel, and a farm parcel with buildings on it now show in the 'Land warnings' column. v1.1's version removed 3 of Luke's 19 Yes corners.
3. Each trade area names one more corner to search: the best-scoring nearby corner that has no usable raw parcel in the tax data (redevelopment land), in 'Also search'.
4. Trade areas (corners within 3 miles of each other, up to 3 corners each) stay from v1.1. Luke's verdicts carry over in grey columns.
limits: • Weights were tuned against Luke's 50 answers, then checked against the 74 7-Elevens built in the pilot counties since 2018: those stores rank at the 74th percentile (v1.0: 76th). Traffic-heavy scoring also lifts older urban 7-Eleven locations, which may not reflect today's strategy.
• Tested and NOT adopted: scoring 'signal unknown' at a quarter instead of half credit. New 7-Elevens are often on county roads FDOT doesn't track for signals, so it pushed them down.
• Luke says a 7-Eleven is already at Silver Palm Blvd & SR-52 (Pasco); our store data (FDEP tanks + 7-Eleven's store list, Oct 31/Nov 11) shows none within 2.7 mi. Need the address to fix the source.
• NWI wetlands are mapped from aerials that can be decades old. The tax roll is as of Jan 1, 2026, so corners built since then still look vacant.
review_readme.sources: FL Dept. of Revenue 2026 final tax roll and parcel maps; FDOT 2025 AADT, functional classification, signals, medians and 2025 rail layers; USFWS National Wetlands Inventory; AllThePlaces store runs Oct 10/17/31 2026; FDEP registered storage tanks; ECP 7-Eleven sales tracker 11/11/26. All pulled or rebuilt 2026-11-17.
review_readme.proposed_extra: • Weights: traffic 35, new homes 25, gap 5. • Removal only below 1.0 ac near the corner. • Extra corners in a trade area must score at least 60% of its best corner.
